title: The reduced neutral component of a bounded p-power torsion group has nontrivial p-kernel
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. All groups are affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Assume $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and every element of $k$ is a $p$-th power. Let $C$ be smooth, connected, commutative and nontrivial ($C\not\simeq\operatorname{Spec}k$). Suppose $[p^e]_C=0$ for some integer $e\geq1$, where $[m]_C$ sends a section $c$ to its $m$-fold sum. Let $H=\ker([p]_C:C\to C)$ be the scheme-theoretic kernel, that is the fibre over the identity section [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $K=(H_{\mathrm{red}})^\circ$, where $H_{\mathrm{red}}$ is the reduced closed subscheme obtained by quotienting the coordinate algebra by its nilpotent elements [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and the superscript denotes the connected component containing the identity. Then $K$ is a nontrivial smooth connected closed subgroup scheme of $C$, is commutative, and $[p]_K=0$.

source.place: Corollary 14.55 proof, printed p.297, the subgroup (U double-prime)_red^0; Corollary 1.39, printed p.18, and Propositions 1.34 and 1.52 on identity components. The nontriviality of this reduced p-kernel, implicit in 14.55, is made explicit under the bounded-exponent hypothesis.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup], $H=\ker[p]_C$ is a closed subgroup of $C$. The affine closed-immersion criterion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] writes $H=\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ when $C=\operatorname{Spec}A$. A finite generating family for $A$ maps to one for $A/J$ and its further quotient by nilpotents, so $H$ and $H_{\mathrm{red}}$ are affine of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply the reduction clause of [lem-sfb-perfect-field-groupoid-image-closure] to the group $H$, viewed as a groupoid on $\operatorname{Spec}k$ with source and target its structure map and composition its multiplication [def-a1-groupoid-scheme, def-sc-group-scheme]. The hypothesis holds because the assumed surjectivity of $a\mapsto a^p$ makes $k$ perfect. Thus $H_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow H$ is a subgroup homomorphism as well as the canonical closed immersion [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction].

source.place: Corollary 14.55, printed p.297, reduced neutral p-kernel; Corollary 1.39 and Proposition 1.34, pp.16-18. The minimal-exponent factorization makes the implicit nontriviality argument explicit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-type-group-identity-subgroup] to $G=H_{\mathrm{red}}$, which is a finite-type group over the given field; algebraic closedness is unnecessary. It gives the connected clopen subgroup $K$ with its open-subscheme structure and a closed immersion $K\hookrightarrow H_{\mathrm{red}}$. Composing with $H_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow H\hookrightarrow C$ gives a closed subgroup of $C$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] to $K\hookrightarrow H_{\mathrm{red}}$: $K$ is affine with coordinate algebra a quotient of that of $H_{\mathrm{red}}$, hence finitely generated over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Since $K$ is also an open subscheme of the reduced scheme $H_{\mathrm{red}}$, its local rings are the same reduced local rings [def-pc-reduced-scheme].

source.place: Corollary 14.55, printed p.297, reduced neutral p-kernel; Corollary 1.39 and Proposition 1.34, pp.16-18. The minimal-exponent factorization makes the implicit nontriviality argument explicit.

proof.text: The reduced finite-type $k$-scheme $K$ is geometrically reduced by [lem-kun-geometric-reduced-perfect], since $k$ is perfect. As $K$ is a group scheme, [lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth] proves that $K$ is smooth. For every $k$-algebra $R$, the inclusion $K(R)\hookrightarrow C(R)$ is an injective homomorphism by [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Its image is commutative and lies in $H(R)=\ker[p]_{C(R)}$ by [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup]. Therefore $K(R)$ is commutative and $[p]_{K(R)}=0$, compatibly with every $R$; these are exactly commutativity of $K$ and the identity $[p]_K=0$ of group-scheme maps.

source.place: Corollary 14.55, printed p.297, reduced neutral p-kernel; Corollary 1.39 and Proposition 1.34, pp.16-18. The minimal-exponent factorization makes the implicit nontriviality argument explicit.

proof.text:
It remains to prove $K
ot\simeq\operatorname{Spec}k$. Choose the least $n\geq1$ with $[p^n]_C=0$; the hypothesis supplies one. Put $a=[p^{n-1}]_C$. If $n>1$, minimality gives $a
e0$; if $n=1$, then $a=[1]_C=\mathrm{id}_C
e0$, since $\mathrm{id}_C=0$ would make the structure morphism and identity section inverse isomorphisms $C\simeq\operatorname{Spec}k$. On sections, $[p]\circ a=[p^n]=0$, so the kernel fibre product gives $b:C	o H$ with composite $a:C	o C$ [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup, def-sc-group-scheme].

source.place: Corollary 14.55, printed p.297, reduced neutral p-kernel; Corollary 1.39 and Proposition 1.34, pp.16-18. The minimal-exponent factorization makes the implicit nontriviality argument explicit.

proof.text: By [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], the smooth scheme $C/k$ is geometrically reduced (it is the fibre over the only point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$), hence reduced. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] to $b:C\to H$: it factors as $b_{\mathrm{red}}:C\to H_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow H$. The lift sends the identity to the identity, since its composite does and the reduction inclusion is a monomorphism. Its continuous image is connected: any decomposition of that image into two nonempty relatively clopen pieces would pull back to such a decomposition of the connected space $C$ [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Hence the image lies in the maximal connected subset of $H_{\mathrm{red}}$ containing the identity, namely $|K|$. Because $K$ is open, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] factors $b_{\mathrm{red}}$ through $K$. If $K\simeq\operatorname{Spec}k$, this factorization makes $a$ the constant identity map: the identity section of $K$ is then the inverse of its structure morphism. This contradicts $a\ne0$ from step 4. Thus $K$ is nontrivial.

lean.statement: theorem exists_nontrivial_reduced_neutral_p_kernel_of_bounded_exponent (k : Type u) [Field k] (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p) (hperfect : Function.Surjective (fun a : k => a ^ p)) (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [GrpObj C] [IsCommMonObj C] [IsAffine C.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [QuasiCompact C.hom] [Smooth C.hom] [ConnectedSpace C.left] (hC : ¬ IsIso C.hom) (e : ℕ) (he : 1 ≤ e) (hexponent : 𝟙 C ^ (p ^ e) = 1) : ∃ (K : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (_ : GrpObj K) (j : K ⟶ GrpObj.ker (𝟙 C ^ p)), IsClosedImmersion j.left ∧ j.left.ker = Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal ⟨connectedComponent (GrpObj.onePoint (GrpObj.ker (𝟙 C ^ p))), isClosed_connectedComponent⟩ ∧ IsClosedSubgroupScheme (j ≫ GrpObj.kerι (𝟙 C ^ p)) ∧ IsAffine K.left ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType K.hom ∧ QuasiCompact K.hom ∧ IsReduced K.left ∧ ¬ IsIso K.hom ∧ Smooth K.hom ∧ ConnectedSpace K.left ∧ IsCommMonObj K ∧ 𝟙 K ^ p = 1
lean.note: K is specified up to its unique isomorphism over H by a closed immersion j into H = ker[p] and the exact vanishing ideal of the identity component of H. This is the reduced induced closed structure, hence precisely (H_red)^0; reduction is a homeomorphism and the component is clopen. The group structure is supplied existentially on this specified scheme, with its canonical inclusion into C a closed subgroup homomorphism. No arbitrary subgroup or map substitutes for K.
